To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use are important determinants of continuance intention in microblogging services.
perceived usefulness, satisfaction, and habit are strong determinants of Twitter use continuance.
perceived usefulness, satisfaction, habit and critical masses are significant predictors of continuance intention in microblogging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why Twitter has become a popular microblogging platform.
the continuance of microblogging services.
the question of why users continue to use microblogging services, in spite of their limitations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study has shown that the use continuance model for Twitter is strongly determined by habit and satisfaction, and that the perceived critical mass of users does not influence use continuance behavior.
the study has shown that Twitter is a service that has been designed to meet the users needs and is therefore a successful microblogging service.
the study provides evidence that perceived usefulness, perceived enjoyment, perceived ease of use and habit have a positive effect on continued use intention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study has identified a set of factors that influence Twitter user continuance behavior.
the study has developed and tested a model of continuance behavior for microblogging services, which is a new area of inquiry for the field of Information Systems research.
we are the first to develop a model of micro-blogging use continuance and that we provide empirical evidence for the model’s validity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microblogging is not a fad and that it is not just for the young.
microblogging use continues because users find it useful, they are satisfied with the service and they are used to it.
Twitter use continues due to the perceived usefulness of the service and the habit that users have developed over time.
